audience.programmeDescription: VU Human Movement Sciences studies how the body and nervous system produce and control movement. It combines anatomy, physiology, biomechanics, neuroscience, psychology, measurement and data analysis to investigate sport, health and rehabilitation.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers genuine study of anatomy, muscular and organ physiology, perception and action, neurobiology, health and quantitative research. Robotics adds kinematic modelling, while mathematics, signal analysis and materials mechanics provide relevant tools. Together these form a broader body-and-brain or quantitative-health programme. Its sustained advanced work would focus on general cognition, health research and mathematical or robotic systems, rather than investigating human movement through linked muscle and force models, measured gait or performance, exercise response and motor adaptation. These foundations are valuable, but do not establish a sufficiently close complete UCR response to this degree.

curriculum.limitation: The 180-EC programme contains 120 EC of required first- and second-year courses, a further 6-EC anatomy course, 30 EC of open choice and a 24-EC research project. No particular optional sport, health or clinical minor is assumed. The research project requires all first-year courses, a passed Statistics course, the passed practical assessment in Measuring Physical Quantities and at least 4.0 on its written examination. Research is conducted in teams of at least two, with an individual report and a joint presentation and defence; the individual report has a second assessor. The proposal must be approved before measurements begin. Required practicals and assignments apply to the relevant courses. The Dutch diagnostic test and any required remediation add no separate credits. The ordinary first-year study-advice threshold is 42 EC, with the specified minimum examination results in Biomechanics and Mathematics, subject to exceptions. Open choice is subject to level, approval and overlap rules; free electives require at least 12 EC at level 300, while an individually composed minor must be coherent and contain no more than one introductory course.
